SpecForge

Rules for building software with AI coding agents

Coding, spec, audit and documentation rules, added to a project with one command: a project with no code yet, or one long in production. Every coding agent gets the same rules, and a check in CI enforces them.

Stacks
Laravel, ASP.NET Core, Next.js, React and Vue, in any combination per project
Agents
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Antigravity, Gemini CLI and Kiro
Needs
Bash 3.2 or later, curl, tar and POSIX tools. Git is optional.

1Install

From the project directory, new or existing:

curl -fsSL https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/install.sh | bash

The installer first detects the project's apps and their stacks, the coding agents already set up and the code host. It then asks five questions, each defaulting to what it found. It installs the rules your answers select, generates each chosen agent's rule files, and records what it did in .ai/specforge.lock.

It never overwrites a file the project already has: the kit's version is written beside it as <file>.specforge-incoming. It never creates application code, CI or a README, and it never commits.

Read it before you run it

curl -fsSLo install.sh https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/install.sh
less install.sh
bash install.sh --dry-run

Without questions

For CI, or for a second project with the same architecture:

cat > rules.answers <<'EOF'
state=existing
app=. laravel
app=resources/js vue
agents=claude cursor
gherkin=no
host=github
EOF
curl -fsSL https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/install.sh | bash -s -- --answers rules.answers

A project's .ai/specforge.lock is itself a valid answers file.

2Hand over to an agent

Open the project in any of your agents and say one of these:

The project has no code yet

Run the bootstrap prompt.

The project already has code

Run the adopt prompt.

Bootstrap asks for the product, the stacks, the shape of the system and your constraints, and drafts the first decisions. Adopt reads the code first, records what exists, runs baseline audits and asks only what the code cannot settle. Both end with a phase-gate report.

3Switch on enforcement

  • Accept or amend the proposed ADRs, and set the Phase line in AGENTS.md from the gate report.
  • Add .ai/bin/check to CI, beside each app's lint, type check and tests.
  • Commit the rules together with .ai/specforge.lock.

4Keep the rules current

Bring the rules to the latest release. Only files still as the kit installed them are replaced; a file you changed stays yours.

curl -fsSL https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/update.sh | bash

Answer the questions again, to add a stack or change the agents:

curl -fsSL https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/update.sh | bash -s -- --reconfigure

Take the rules back out. Every file still unmodified is removed; a file you changed is kept:

curl -fsSL https://shakilnwz.github.io/specforge/uninstall.sh | bash

5Options

Options follow bash -s -- when a script is piped, and each script lists its own with --help.

OptionScriptsEffect
--dir DIRallThe project directory; the current one by default
--dry-runallPrint what would change, and change nothing
--answers FILEinstall, updateTake the answers from a file instead of asking
--yesinstallAsk nothing; take what detection found
--reconfigureupdateAsk the questions again
--version vX.Y.Zinstall, updateUse that release instead of the script's own

To pin a release, take its scripts from https://github.com/shakilnwz/specforge/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/install.sh, and likewise update.sh and uninstall.sh.
